segments.text: God, if anyone can build an app in a weekend now, what's actually becoming valuable?
Not the app.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: The people waiting for it.
Wait, the app isn't the valuable part?
Over half a million new apps hit the App Store in just six months this year.
That's almost as many as all of last year, but downloads only went up 2%.
So everybody's building and nobody's downloading?
Picture two taco trucks.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Same tacos.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: One has a line of people down the street.
tone: a person speaking in a flat deadpan monotone

segments.text: Anyone can make tacos now.
The line is the valuable part.
Okay, but how do I get a line?
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: I have like nine followers.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: You don't need millions.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: You need a few hundred people with the same problem.
Step one, pick one kind of person and one problem you know well, like parents with picky
eaters.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: How do I find out what they need?
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Step two, in the Claude app, ask me to find what parents of picky eaters complain about
most online.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: I search and hand you their top 10 problems in their own words.
Then I build the app.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: That's the mistake everybody makes.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: They build for months, then launch to nobody.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Step three, post one free tip for them every day.
I can turn each problem into a short video script.
Why give it away for free?
Free help is how strangers start to trust you.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Trust is what builds the line at your taco truck.
Step four, get them on an email list.
Kit is free for your first 10,000 people.
Why email?
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: I already have followers.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Followers are rented.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Instagram can change its rules any day.
Your email list is yours.
Kit gives you a free sign up page.
Put its link in your Instagram bio.
Okay, now do I build the app?
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Almost.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Here's the tip most people skip.
Sell it before you build it.
Sell an app that doesn't even exist yet?
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: Ask me for one screen of it.
Email a screenshot to your list.
Sell early access in Kit for $5.
They pay now and get it first.
If 10 people pay, we build the rest this weekend.
If nobody pays, you just saved a month.
So the app is the easy part now?
Anyone can make the tacos.
Not everyone has the line.
Okay, one free tip every day.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: I'm starting next Monday.
tone: a confused person asking a question

segments.text: You said that last Monday.
Ask me anything.
